title: The granny square
subtitle: A four-round motif worked in the round — the foundation of a hundred pattern uses
excerpt: The traditional granny square is four rounds worked into a chain ring, building corner chain spaces and treble clusters. It is the entry point for motif crochet: joinable, portable, and useful in every size from coaster to blanket.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet — the square motif pattern, first published in the late Victorian series. Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886).

glossaryTerms.definition: A group of three treble stitches worked into the same space, with their tops joined into one. The basic building block of the granny square's side panels.
The ch-2 space at each corner of a granny square, worked between two treble clusters. Corner chain spaces are used in subsequent rounds to build the square outward.

content.text: The traditional granny square is four rounds: a chain ring centre, four corner
. Each additional round adds one more cluster to each side. The same structure scales from a small coaster (3 rounds) to a full blanket section (12+ rounds).
The pattern (4 rounds, DK cotton, 4 mm hook)
Ch 4, join with a sl st to form a ring.
Round 1: Ch 3 (counts as first tr), 2 tr into ring, ch 2 (first corner space). *3 tr into ring, ch 2. Repeat from * twice more. Join with sl st to top of ch-3. (4 clusters, 4 corner spaces.)

Round 2: Sl st into first corner space. Ch 3, 2 tr into same corner space, ch 2, 3 tr into same corner space (first corner made). *3 tr into side space between clusters, then into next corner space work [3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr] (corner made). Repeat from * twice more. 3 tr into remaining side space. Join with sl st. (8 clusters, 4 corner spaces.)
Round 3: Work as Round 2, adding one more 3-tr cluster per side (into the ch-1 space between clusters). Each side now has 2 clusters; each corner has the standard [3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr]. (12 clusters.)
Round 4: Repeat the same pattern. Each side now has 3 clusters; each corner unchanged. Fasten off and sew in tails. (16 clusters.)

Each round can be a different colour. Join the new colour with a slip stitch at the corner space at the start of each new round; fasten off and weave in at the end. For a tidy join, start each new colour with a standing treble instead of a ch-3.

Granny squares are usually joined after completing all the individual squares. Three standard joins: whipstitch through back loops (soft, visible seam), slip-stitch seam (raised seam as a design feature), or join-as-you-go during the final round. The whipstitch join is the easiest for a first blanket.
